title: CLAP: Cross-Embodiment Video World Models are Zero-Shot Physical Simulators
abstract: arXiv:2608.27406v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: State-of-the-art action-conditioned video models are typically restricted to a single robot embodiment, preventing them from leveraging the vast corpus of heterogeneous video data that contains rich signals for learning generalizable physics. To bridge this gap, we introduce CLAP, a framework for cross-embodiment action-conditioned video generation capable of being trained on diverse, internet-scale videos across human and robotic agents. CLAP is grounded in the insight that universal physical laws govern spatiotemporal dynamics regardless of the actor. However, cross-embodiment learning is non-trivial because action representations vary sharply across robot platforms and are typically absent in human videos. CLAP addresses this fundamental challenge through the following core contributions. First, CLAP reconciles disparate action spaces using end-effector poses, language instructions, and latent actions. translated_title: CLAP：跨形态视频世界模型是零样本物理模拟器
translated_abstract: 最先进的基于动作条件的视频模型通常局限于单一机器人形态，这阻碍了它们利用包含丰富信号的大规模异构视频数据来学习可泛化的物理规律。为弥合这一差距，我们引入了CLAP，一个跨形态动作条件视频生成框架，能够在人类和机器人代理的多样化互联网规模视频上进行训练。CLAP基于一个洞察：无论行动者是谁，普遍的物理规律都支配着时空动态。然而，跨形态学习并非易事，因为不同机器人平台的动作表示差异巨大，且人类视频中通常缺少这些动作。CLAP通过以下核心贡献解决了这一根本性挑战。首先，CLAP使用末端执行器姿态、语言指令和潜在动作来协调不同的动作空间。其次，为解决它们的不可分割性，[摘要在此处截断]
tldr: CLAP提出了一种跨形态视频生成框架，利用末端执行器姿态、语言指令和潜在动作统一不同机器人平台的动作表示，实现在人类和机器人视频上的零样本物理模拟。
en_tdlr: CLAP proposes a cross-embodiment video generation framework that unifies action representations across robot platforms using end-effector poses, language instructions, and latent actions, enabling zero-shot physical simulation on human and robot videos.
